staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the saved AddressSanitizer crash against this staged fwupd checkout.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42534457 (fwupd): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 found by fuzz target uswid_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42534457
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / staged poc bytes
bug_description.normalized: The staged 439-byte witness is a uSWID blob whose payload is handed to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse()` as CBOR. The inner coSWID root contains `PAYLOAD -> FILE -> HASH`; in the staged bytes the `HASH` field starts as an outer indefinite array whose first element is a valid 2-item hash tuple `[1, <36-byte bytestring>]`, and after that tuple's bytestring ends at offset `0x143` the next outer element begins at offset `0x144` as the non-array CBOR text item `65 6E 2D 55 53 08` (length 5; payload bytes `6E 2D 55 53 08`). `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` decides between `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash_array()` and `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` only by inspecting element 0, so the array-looking first element routes the entire outer array to `parse_hash_array`. On the next iteration that extracts that later text item, `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` immediately executes `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` before checking `cbor_isa_array(item)`. That direct call site passes a text-string CBOR item to libcbor's array accessor; `cbor_array_get` then performs the saved `READ of size 8` from the 5-byte heap region allocated for the string by `cbor_builder_string_callback`, and AddressSanitizer reports heap-buffer-overflow in `cbor_array_get`. The staged patch fixes this exact missing obligation by rejecting non-array `item` before either `cbor_array_get` call in `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()`.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled coSWID payload into the CBOR item graph later traversed by the vulnerable hash parser.
source.value_from: The staged 439-byte `poc` is a uSWID blob; `fu_uswid_firmware_parse()` slices its embedded payload and later calls the inner coSWID parser on it. In the staged bytes the coSWID subtree containing the crash includes `... 07 9F 82 01 58 24 <36 bytes> 65 6E 2D 55 53 08 ...`, which under the `fu-coswid.rs` tag numbering is the `HASH` field of `PAYLOAD -> FILE`: the outer hash array starts with a valid `[1, <36-byte bytestring>]` tuple, the tuple's bytestring content runs through offset `0x143`, and the next outer element starts at `0x144` as a non-array 5-byte text item. The saved ASan allocation stack shows this `cbor_load()` path allocating that 5-byte string node via `cbor_builder_string_callback`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Immediate origin of the `item` argument later misused by `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()`. On the crashing iteration, this extracts the next outer-hash element, which starts at offset `0x144` as the non-array CBOR text item `65 6E 2D 55 53 08` (length 5; payload bytes `6E 2D 55 53 08`), not a hash tuple array.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` assumes its `item` parameter is always a CBOR array and calls `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` before verifying `cbor_isa_array(item)`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (!cbor_isa_array(item))` before this line and before the matching `cbor_array_get(item, 1)` call.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink at the direct project call site. This statement invokes libcbor's array accessor on the non-array `item` from the mixed-shape `HASH` array.
sink.note: The saved ASan report attributes the actual invalid read to `cbor_array_get` in `libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23`, where the accessor performs an 8-byte read from the 5-byte heap region backing the text string passed here.

parser_admitted.description: The outer uSWID header has already been accepted, the embedded payload has been sliced into `fw2`, and control is now entering the inner coSWID parser on attacker-controlled payload bytes.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is closed from the staged bytes, vulnerable source, patch, saved ASan traces, and reproduction report only.

Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though `patch.diff` adds the exact missing `cbor_isa_array(item)` guard before the crashing call.

The staged workspace contains fwupd sources but not the libcbor checkout. This GT therefore anchors the top-level sink at the direct project call site `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash:223` and records the actual ASan crash location separately as `cbor_array_get` in `libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23`.

coarse_trace.summary: The libFuzzer harness wraps the exact 439-byte witness in `GBytes` and calls `fu_firmware_parse()` on a `FuUswidFirmware` object.
fwupd accepts the outer uSWID container, slices one embedded payload chunk, and calls the inner coSWID parser on attacker-controlled payload bytes.
The inner payload is decoded as CBOR and the root tag loop routes through `PAYLOAD -> FILE -> HASH` into the file parser.

The file parser checks only that `HASH` is a non-empty outer array and that element 0 is itself an array; because the first element looks like a valid hash tuple, it dispatches the entire outer array to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash_array()`.

On the next `parse_hash_array()` iteration the outer `HASH` array yields the later non-array text item that begins at offset `0x144` as `65 6E 2D 55 53 08`; `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` still calls `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` as if that item were an array, and AddressSanitizer reports heap-buffer-overflow in libcbor.

fine_trace.note: Source. After `fu_uswid_firmware_parse()` slices the inner payload, `cbor_load()` materializes the attacker-controlled coSWID bytes into a CBOR object graph. The saved allocation stack shows this decode allocating the later 5-byte text-string node that will be misused as a hash array element.

The decoded root map reaches the `FU_COSWID_TAG_PAYLOAD` entry and forwards its value into `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_one_or_many()`. This payload subtree contains the malformed `FILE -> HASH` structure that later reaches the sink.
The witness encodes the top-level `PAYLOAD` value as an array, so `parse_one_or_many()` takes the array arm and extracts one payload map `value` for `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_payload()`.

Inside that payload map, the loop reaches the `FU_COSWID_TAG_FILE` entry and forwards its value toward the file parser. In the witness this file value is already a map, so `parse_one_or_many()` immediately enters `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` on that same subtree.
The file's `HASH` field passes only an outer-container check: it must be an array with at least one element. No validation here proves that every outer-array element is itself a hash tuple array.
The parser extracts the first outer `HASH` element. In the staged bytes this first element is the definite 2-item array `[1, <36-byte bytestring>]`, so it looks like a valid hash tuple.

Because that first outer element is itself an array, the parser assumes the entire outer `HASH` value is an array of hash arrays and dispatches the full outer array to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash_array()`. This decision is based only on element 0 and ignores the shapes of later elements.

On the next `parse_hash_array()` iteration after the valid tuple, `value` becomes the next outer `HASH` element. The first tuple's 36-byte bytestring runs through offset `0x143`, and the extracted element starts at `0x144` as CBOR text item `65 6E 2D 55 53 08`, i.e. a 5-byte text item with payload bytes `6E 2D 55 53 08`, not an array. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` receives this `value` as its `item` parameter.

Root cause and sink. `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()` immediately calls `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` before any `cbor_isa_array(item)` guard. Here `item` is the non-array 5-byte text item from step 8, so libcbor treats that 5-byte string allocation as array storage and AddressSanitizer reports `READ of size 8` at `libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23` on address `0x602000001990`, 0 bytes to the right of region `[0x602000001990, 0x602000001995)`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the exact missing `if (!cbor_isa_array(item))` guard in `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()`, but Stage 02 does not execute the fixed image.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: The saved ASan top frame is libcbor `cbor_array_get` at `libcbor/src/cbor/arrays.c:23`, and fine-trace step 9 is the direct caller-side statement `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` at `libfwupdplugin/fu-coswid-firmware.c:223` that triggers that library read.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run feeds the exact staged 439-byte corpus file (sha256 `5b221b8a24ffe364f2185edd3853baa69f4c8244a027a44c51098598a5a03c11`) to `uswid_fuzzer`; the run reproduces `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` with the saved stack `cbor_array_get -> fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash -> fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash_array`.

format.name: uSWID with embedded coSWID CBOR
format.contract: A uSWID blob whose embedded coSWID `PAYLOAD -> FILE -> HASH` field is an outer array where element 0 is a valid 2-item hash tuple array `[alg_id, bytes]`, and the next outer element starts at offset `0x144` as the non-array CBOR text item `65 6E 2D 55 53 08` (length 5; payload bytes `6E 2D 55 53 08`). That exact mixed-shape outer `HASH` array forces `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_file()` down the `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash_array()` path and then hands the non-array text item to `fu_coswid_firmware_parse_hash()`, which immediately calls `cbor_array_get(item, 0)` on it. This GT does not generalize beyond that witnessed mixed-shape outer array.
